direction_notes: Direct US bursts to motor cortex excited hindlimb/scrotum movement (excitatory), while concurrent US significantly suppressed the long-term epidural-cortical-stimulation-evoked motor response (inhibitory); short-term (single paired-pulse) modulation of the ECS response was not significant.
safety_notes: US heating in motor cortex averaged 1.8 +/- 0.6 degC (peak ~3 degC) using a cortical thermocouple; no gross behavioral changes from repeated stimulation were observed.

exposures.label: US stimulation of motor cortex (US/ECS interaction and EMG-latency protocols)

timing.protocol_description: The US power was delivered in bursts of 500-us pulses every 1 ms (50% duty at a 1-kHz pulse rate). For the US-ECS interaction experiment, the 50% duty US bursts were 300 ms in duration at 0.5 Hz. For the EMG latency measurement, the US bursts were only 3 ms (4 pulses), repeated every 10 s. Burst interval for the US/ECS interaction experiment ranged 1-10 s (mean 2 s, Table 1).

source_quotes.exposures[0].fundamental_frequency_khz: The 200-kHz US frequency was chosen because lower frequencies appear to be more effective for stimulating motor cortex (Kim et al. 2014; Ye et al. 2016).
source_quotes.exposures[0].free_field.ispta_w_cm2: For the US–ECS interaction experiment, the 50% duty US bursts were 300 ms in duration at 0.5 Hz, giving an SPTA (spatial peak time average) power of 4.5 W/cm<sup>2</sup>. For the EMG latency measurement, the US bursts were only 3 ms (4 pulses), repeated every 10 s, giving a 9 mW/cm<sup>2</sup> SPTA (Table 1).

source_quotes.n_sessions_per_subject: Four male Sprague-Dawley rats were implanted with epidural arrays and tested over multiple sessions (up to three sessions per rat).
source_quotes.n_subjects: Four male Sprague-Dawley rats were implanted with epidural arrays and tested over multiple sessions (up to three sessions per rat).

flags.reason: Paper never states a single total: 4 array-implanted rats were used for the modulation/direct-response experiments, a separate group of 3 non-implanted rats was used only for temperature measurement, and EMG latency was measured in 2-3 rats (unclear overlap with the primary 4); left not_reported rather than guess a sum.
Paper reports 'SPTP' (spatial-peak time-peak) rather than the conventional ISPPA (spatial-peak pulse-average); mapped to isppa_w_cm2 as the closest standard quantity.

The 100 W/cm2 power density was derived from a water-tank hydrophone/force-balance calibration, then applied in vivo through a craniotomy with no skull in the beam path; recorded as free_field since the paper never states an independently measured or simulated in-brain value.
Study has no designed sham/placebo arm for TUS itself; the 'no-US' ECS-only blocks were used as the comparison condition, classified here as no_treatment_control as the closest vocabulary fit.
Randomisation described is of trial order (which ECS pulses were preceded by a US burst) within-subject, not random allocation of subjects to groups.
